"""Synthetic coordinated campaigns and organic look-alikes, injected IN MEMORY into a window.

Nothing here is ever posted anywhere or written to the live database: everything is generated
locally, seeded and reproducible, and every synthetic DID starts with `did:plc:synth`.

Difficulty levels (what a campaign does inside the window):
  L1  copy-paste text + same link, brand-new templated accounts, tight burst (< 1 min),
      and the accounts co-like the same promoted posts within a minute
  L2  paraphrased text (1-2 words swapped per slot), accounts 3-8 weeks old,
      timing jittered over ~5 minutes, co-likes jittered over a few minutes
  L3  heavy paraphrase, aged accounts with followers on diverse PDSes, slow drip over the whole
      window, each account also doing unrelated organic-looking likes

Hard negatives (organic look-alikes that must NOT come out `coordinated`):
  viral       thousands of established accounts liking one post
  news_link   dozens of established accounts sharing the same news URL with their own words
  live_event  a burst of short, varied posts with the same hashtag (live TV / sports)
  fandom      established fans liking the same handful of posts at their own pace
"""

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import numpy as np

from signals.score import AccountInfo
from signals.textnorm import text_hash
from signals.window import WAction, WindowData, WPost

SYNTH_PREFIX = "did:plc:synth"

_WORDS = ["amber", "nova", "pixel", "river", "echo", "lumen", "orbit", "maple", "cobalt", "delta"]
_TEMPLATE = [
    ["Huge", "Massive", "Incredible"],
    ["news:", "update:", "alert:"],
    ["the new", "this new", "the latest"],
    ["policy", "plan", "proposal"],
    ["will", "is going to", "could"],
    ["destroy", "ruin", "wreck"],
    ["our local", "your local", "every local"],
    ["economy", "jobs", "businesses"],
    ["read", "see", "check"],
    ["the full story", "the real story", "what they hide"],
    ["before it gets deleted", "before they delete it", "while you still can"],
]
_L3_SENTENCES = [
    "Not sure people realise what this policy means for small towns.",
    "Honestly the policy everyone is cheering will hurt local shops the most.",
    "Did anyone actually read the fine print on this plan? Local jobs are toast.",
    "My neighbour runs a bakery and says this proposal would finish her off.",
    "Funny how nobody on TV talks about what the plan does to local businesses.",
    "Small business owners are terrified of this, and nobody is listening.",
]
_ORGANIC_SHORT = [
    "what a goal",
    "unbelievable",
    "no way",
    "this is insane",
    "lets go",
    "i cant watch",
    "ref is blind",
    "amazing scenes",
    "wow",
    "tears",
]


def _did(tag: str, i: int, seed: int) -> str:
    h = hashlib.blake2b(f"{tag}|{seed}|{i}".encode(), digest_size=10).hexdigest()
    return f"{SYNTH_PREFIX}{tag}{h}"[:32]


def _post_uri(did: str, n: int) -> str:
    return f"at://{did}/app.bsky.feed.post/synth{n:06d}"


@dataclass
class Synthetic:
    name: str
    coordinated: bool  # ground truth label
    posts: list[WPost] = field(default_factory=list)
    actions: list[WAction] = field(default_factory=list)
    accounts: dict[str, AccountInfo] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def dids(self) -> set[str]:
        return set(self.accounts)


def _info(
    did: str,
    rng,
    age: tuple[float, float],
    followers: tuple[int, int],
    *,
    handle: str,
    avatar: bool,
    desc: int,
    pds: str,
) -> AccountInfo:
    return AccountInfo(
        did=did,
        handle=handle,
        display_name=handle.split(".")[0],
        age_days=float(rng.uniform(*age)),
        followers=int(rng.integers(*followers)),
        follows=int(rng.integers(0, 300)),
        posts_count=int(rng.integers(5, 3000)),
        description_len=desc,
        has_avatar=avatar,
        pds_host=pds,
        handle_changes=0,
    )


def campaign(level: str, wd: WindowData, seed: int = 0, n_accounts: int = 12) -> Synthetic:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    s = Synthetic(name=f"campaign_{level}_s{seed}", coordinated=True)
    span = wd.end - wd.start
    link = f"https://synth-news-{seed}.example/story"
    promoted = [f"at://did:plc:synthtarget{seed:04d}/app.bsky.feed.post/p{k}" for k in range(4)]
    if level == "L1":
        t0 = wd.start + rng.uniform(0.2, 0.7) * span
        times = t0 + rng.uniform(0, 30, n_accounts)
        like_times = lambda i, k: t0 + 40 + rng.uniform(0, 50)  # noqa: E731
    elif level == "L2":
        t0 = wd.start + rng.uniform(0.1, 0.5) * span
        times = t0 + rng.uniform(0, 300, n_accounts)
        like_times = lambda i, k: t0 + rng.uniform(0, 240)  # noqa: E731
    elif level == "L3":
        times = wd.start + rng.uniform(0, span, n_accounts)
        like_times = lambda i, k: wd.start + rng.uniform(0, span)  # noqa: E731
    else:
        raise ValueError(level)
    for i in range(n_accounts):
        did = _did(level.lower(), i, seed)
        word = _WORDS[(seed + i) % len(_WORDS)]
        if level == "L1":
            info = _info(
                did,
                rng,
                (1, 10),
                (0, 4),
                handle=f"{word}{rng.integers(1000, 9999)}.bsky.social",
                avatar=False,
                desc=0,
                pds="synthpds.example",
            )
            text = " ".join(opts[0] for opts in _TEMPLATE)
        elif level == "L2":
            info = _info(
                did,
                rng,
                (20, 60),
                (2, 40),
                handle=f"{word}{rng.integers(10, 99)}.bsky.social",
                avatar=bool(rng.random() < 0.5),
                desc=int(rng.integers(0, 40)),
                pds="morel.us-east.host.bsky.network",
            )
            words = [opts[0] for opts in _TEMPLATE]
            for slot in rng.choice(len(_TEMPLATE), size=2, replace=False):
                words[slot] = _TEMPLATE[slot][int(rng.integers(0, 3))]
            text = " ".join(words)
        else:
            info = _info(
                did,
                rng,
                (200, 900),
                (60, 900),
                handle=f"{word}{'xyz'[i % 3]}{['writes', 'daily', 'official'][i % 3]}.bsky.social",
                avatar=True,
                desc=int(rng.integers(40, 200)),
                pds=f"pds{i % 4}.us-west.host.bsky.network",
            )
            text = _L3_SENTENCES[i % len(_L3_SENTENCES)]
        s.accounts[did] = info
        uri = _post_uri(did, i)
        s.posts.append(
            WPost(
                uri=uri,
                did=did,
                t=float(times[i]),
                text=text,
                text_hash=text_hash(text),
                embed_urls=[link],
                langs=["en"],
            )
        )
        for k, subj in enumerate(promoted):
            t = float(np.clip(like_times(i, k), wd.start, wd.end - 1))
            s.actions.append(
                WAction(
                    "like",
                    f"at://{did}/app.bsky.feed.like/synth{k}",
                    did,
                    t,
                    subj,
                    subj.split("/")[2],
                )
            )
        if level == "L3":  # unrelated organic-looking likes
            for k in range(6):
                subj = f"at://did:plc:synthrandom{rng.integers(1e9)}/app.bsky.feed.post/r{k}"
                s.actions.append(
                    WAction(
                        "like",
                        f"at://{did}/app.bsky.feed.like/synthr{k}",
                        did,
                        float(wd.start + rng.uniform(0, span)),
                        subj,
                        subj.split("/")[2],
                    )
                )
    return s


_FIRST = [
    "alex",
    "samira",
    "kimberly",
    "jo",
    "leena",
    "maxwell",
    "oskari",
    "priya",
    "tom",
    "ines",
    "yusuf",
    "marta",
    "chen",
    "ola",
    "ravi",
    "zoe",
]
_LAST = ["martin", "berg", "nakamura", "okafor", "virtanen", "silva", "novak", "kaur"]
_DOMAINS = ["bsky.social", "bsky.social", "bsky.social", "example.fi", "example.org"]


def _established(tag: str, i: int, seed: int, rng) -> tuple[str, AccountInfo]:
    """Old, followed accounts with varied, human-looking handles on varied hosts."""
    did = _did(tag, i, seed)
    first, last = _FIRST[int(rng.integers(len(_FIRST)))], _LAST[int(rng.integers(len(_LAST)))]
    style = int(rng.integers(4))
    local = [first, f"{first}{last}", f"{first}-{last}", f"{last}{first[0]}"][style]
    domain = _DOMAINS[int(rng.integers(len(_DOMAINS)))]
    handle = f"{local}.{domain}" if domain == "bsky.social" else f"{first}.{last}{i}.{domain}"
    return did, _info(
        did,
        rng,
        (380, 1000),
        (120, 5000),
        handle=handle,
        avatar=True,
        desc=int(rng.integers(20, 250)),
        pds=f"pds{i % 7}.host.bsky.network",
    )


def hard_negative(kind: str, wd: WindowData, seed: int = 0) -> Synthetic:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(10_000 + seed)
    s = Synthetic(name=f"negative_{kind}_s{seed}", coordinated=False)
    span = wd.end - wd.start
    if kind == "viral":
        subj = f"at://did:plc:synthstar{seed:04d}/app.bsky.feed.post/viral"
        t0 = wd.start + 0.1 * span
        for i in range(5000):
            did, info = _established("vir", i, seed, rng)
            s.accounts[did] = info
            t = float(min(wd.end - 1, t0 + rng.exponential(span / 4)))
            s.actions.append(
                WAction(
                    "like", f"at://{did}/app.bsky.feed.like/v", did, t, subj, subj.split("/")[2]
                )
            )
    elif kind == "news_link":
        link = f"https://synth-bignews-{seed}.example/2026/11/13/story"
        for i in range(60):
            did, info = _established("news", i, seed, rng)
            s.accounts[did] = info
            text = (
                f"{rng.choice(['Wow.', 'Read this.', 'Big if true:', 'Ugh.', 'Finally!'])} "
                f"{rng.choice(_L3_SENTENCES)} {rng.integers(1e6)}"
            )
            s.posts.append(
                WPost(
                    uri=_post_uri(did, i),
                    did=did,
                    t=float(wd.start + rng.uniform(0, span)),
                    text=text,
                    text_hash=text_hash(text),
                    embed_urls=[link],
                    langs=["en"],
                )
            )
    elif kind == "live_event":
        t0 = wd.start + 0.4 * span
        for i in range(40):
            did, info = _established("live", i, seed, rng)
            s.accounts[did] = info
            text = f"{rng.choice(_ORGANIC_SHORT)} #synthfinal"
            s.posts.append(
                WPost(
                    uri=_post_uri(did, i),
                    did=did,
                    t=float(t0 + rng.uniform(0, 120)),
                    text=text,
                    text_hash=text_hash(text),
                    langs=["en"],
                )
            )
    elif kind == "fandom":
        subjects = [f"at://did:plc:synthartist{seed:04d}/app.bsky.feed.post/a{k}" for k in range(5)]
        for i in range(30):
            did, info = _established("fan", i, seed, rng)
            s.accounts[did] = info
            for k, subj in enumerate(subjects):
                if rng.random() < 0.8:
                    s.actions.append(
                        WAction(
                            "like",
                            f"at://{did}/app.bsky.feed.like/f{k}",
                            did,
                            float(wd.start + rng.uniform(0, span)),
                            subj,
                            subj.split("/")[2],
                        )
                    )
    else:
        raise ValueError(kind)
    return s


def inject(wd: WindowData, *synths: Synthetic) -> WindowData:
    """A new WindowData with the synthetic events added (background counts updated too)."""
    out = WindowData(
        start=wd.start,
        end=wd.end,
        posts=list(wd.posts),
        actions=list(wd.actions),
        background={k: v.copy() for k, v in wd.background.items()},
        active_accounts=wd.active_accounts,
    )
    n = max(1, int(round(wd.end - wd.start)))
    for s in synths:
        out.posts.extend(s.posts)
        out.actions.extend(s.actions)
        for kind, times in (
            ("post", [p.t for p in s.posts]),
            *((k, [a.t for a in s.actions if a.kind == k]) for k in ("like", "repost", "follow")),
        ):
            if not times:
                continue
            bg = out.background.setdefault(kind, np.zeros(n))
            idx = np.clip((np.asarray(times) - wd.start).astype(int), 0, n - 1)
            np.add.at(bg, idx, 1)
        out.active_accounts += len(s.accounts)
    return out


def empty_window(
    start: float = 1_800_000_000.0,
    length: float = 600.0,
    seed: int = 0,
    organic_accounts: int = 400,
) -> WindowData:
    """A plain organic background: independent accounts posting unique texts and liking random
    posts at random times. Used by tests when no recorded slice is at hand."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    wd = WindowData(start=start, end=start + length)
    for i in range(organic_accounts):
        did = f"did:plc:bgacct{seed:03d}{i:06d}"
        for j in range(int(rng.integers(1, 4))):
            text = f"organic thought number {i} {j} about {rng.choice(_WORDS)} {rng.integers(1e9)}"
            wd.posts.append(
                WPost(
                    uri=_post_uri(did, j),
                    did=did,
                    t=float(start + rng.uniform(0, length)),
                    text=text,
                    text_hash=text_hash(text),
                    langs=["en"],
                )
            )
        for j in range(int(rng.integers(0, 6))):
            subj = f"at://did:plc:bgauthor{int(rng.integers(0, 3000))}/app.bsky.feed.post/x"
            wd.actions.append(
                WAction(
                    "like",
                    f"at://{did}/app.bsky.feed.like/b{j}",
                    did,
                    float(start + rng.uniform(0, length)),
                    subj,
                    subj.split("/")[2],
                )
            )
    times = {"post": [p.t for p in wd.posts], "like": [a.t for a in wd.actions]}
    wd.background = WindowData.background_from_times(wd.start, wd.end, times)
    wd.active_accounts = organic_accounts
    return wd

"""Detector entry point: window data -> scored clusters. Pure: no DB writes, deterministic.

    from signals.detect import detect
    results = detect(window_data, account_info=lambda dids: {...}, cfg=DEFAULT)

`account_info` is called once with all candidate members and returns {did: AccountInfo} for the
ones it knows (identity family and organic guards need it; pass None to skip them).
"""

import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from signals.config import DEFAULT, DetectorConfig
from signals.graph import build_graph, communities
from signals.keys import MinHashCache, build_keys
from signals.score import AccountInfo, ClusterScore, score_cluster
from signals.window import WindowData

AccountInfoFn = Callable[[list[str]], dict[str, AccountInfo]]


@dataclass
class DetectResult:
    clusters: list[ClusterScore]
    stats: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def detect(
    wd: WindowData,
    account_info: AccountInfoFn | None = None,
    cfg: DetectorConfig = DEFAULT,
    mh_cache: MinHashCache | None = None,
) -> DetectResult:
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    keys = build_keys(wd, cfg, mh_cache)
    t1 = time.monotonic()
    graph = build_graph(keys, cfg)
    groups = communities(graph, cfg)
    t2 = time.monotonic()
    # Pass 1 without account info. Then fetch account info only for clusters where something
    # looked suspicious (strongest first: the enrichment budget is limited) and rescore those.
    clusters = [score_cluster(g, keys, wd, {}, cfg) for g in groups]
    suspicious = sorted(
        (i for i, c in enumerate(clusters) if max(c.family_scores.values()) >= cfg.family_fire),
        key=lambda i: (-clusters[i].score, len(clusters[i].members), clusters[i].members[0]),
    )
    ordered = list(dict.fromkeys(d for i in suspicious for d in clusters[i].members))
    info = account_info(ordered) if account_info and ordered else {}
    t3 = time.monotonic()
    for i in suspicious:
        if any(d in info for d in clusters[i].members):
            clusters[i] = score_cluster(groups[i], keys, wd, info, cfg)
    t4 = time.monotonic()
    by_status: dict[str, int] = {}
    for c in clusters:
        by_status[c.status] = by_status.get(c.status, 0) + 1
    stats = {
        "posts": len(wd.posts),
        "actions": len(wd.actions),
        "keys": len(keys),
        "graph_accounts": len(graph.dids),
        "edges": len(graph.edges),
        "clusters": len(clusters),
        "by_status": by_status,
        "accounts_with_info": len(info),
        "seconds": {
            "keys": round(t1 - t0, 2),
            "graph": round(t2 - t1, 2),
            "score_and_enrich": round(t3 - t2, 2),
            "rescore": round(t4 - t3, 2),
        },
    }
    return DetectResult(clusters, stats)
"""Window data: everything the detector needs for one time window, loaded from Postgres or built
in memory (tests, synthetic campaigns). The detector itself never touches the DB."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime

import numpy as np
import psycopg

from signals.config import DetectorConfig


@dataclass(slots=True)
class WPost:
    uri: str
    did: str
    t: float  # seen_at, epoch seconds
    text: str | None = None
    text_hash: str | None = None
    embed_urls: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    media_hashes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    reply_to: str | None = None
    reply_root: str | None = None
    quote_uri: str | None = None
    created_t: float | None = None  # client createdAt, epoch seconds
    deleted: bool = False
    langs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass(slots=True)
class WAction:
    """A like, repost or follow. subject is a post URI (like/repost) or a DID (follow)."""

    kind: str  # like | repost | follow
    uri: str
    did: str
    t: float
    subject: str
    subject_did: str | None = None
    deleted: bool = False


@dataclass
class WindowData:
    start: float
    end: float
    posts: list[WPost] = field(default_factory=list)
    actions: list[WAction] = field(default_factory=list)
    # Per-second counts of ALL events of each kind in the window (not just loaded ones): the
    # empirical background used by the timing null model. kind -> array of len(end - start).
    background: dict[str, np.ndarray] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # Distinct accounts per kind over the whole stream in the window (for popularity / base rates).
    active_accounts: int = 0

    def background_for(self, kind: str) -> np.ndarray:
        bg = self.background.get(kind)
        n = max(1, int(round(self.end - self.start)))
        if bg is None or len(bg) == 0 or bg.sum() == 0:
            return np.ones(n)
        return bg

    @staticmethod
    def background_from_times(start: float, end: float, times_by_kind: dict[str, list[float]]):
        n = max(1, int(round(end - start)))
        out = {}
        for kind, times in times_by_kind.items():
            idx = np.clip((np.asarray(times, dtype=float) - start).astype(int), 0, n - 1)
            out[kind] = np.bincount(idx, minlength=n).astype(float)
        return out


_POSTS_SQL = """
SELECT DISTINCT ON (uri) uri, did, extract(epoch FROM seen_at)::float8 AS t, text, text_hash,
       embed_urls, media_hashes, reply_to, reply_root, quote_uri,
       extract(epoch FROM created_at)::float8 AS created_t, deleted_at IS NOT NULL AS deleted, langs
FROM posts WHERE seen_at >= %(s)s AND seen_at < %(e)s
ORDER BY uri, seen_at
"""

# Only subjects shared by a non-trivial, non-viral number of accounts can create edges.
_ACTIONS_SQL = """
WITH subj AS (
    SELECT subject_uri FROM {table}
    WHERE seen_at >= %(s)s AND seen_at < %(e)s
    GROUP BY subject_uri
    HAVING count(DISTINCT did) BETWEEN %(lo)s AND %(hi)s
)
SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.uri) a.uri, a.did, extract(epoch FROM a.seen_at)::float8 AS t,
       a.subject_uri, a.subject_did, a.deleted_at IS NOT NULL AS deleted
FROM {table} a JOIN subj USING (subject_uri)
WHERE a.seen_at >= %(s)s AND a.seen_at < %(e)s
ORDER BY a.uri, a.seen_at
"""

_FOLLOWS_SQL = """
WITH subj AS (
    SELECT subject_did FROM follows
    WHERE seen_at >= %(s)s AND seen_at < %(e)s
    GROUP BY subject_did
    HAVING count(DISTINCT did) BETWEEN %(lo)s AND %(hi)s
)
SELECT DISTINCT ON (f.uri) f.uri, f.did, extract(epoch FROM f.seen_at)::float8 AS t,
       f.subject_did, f.deleted_at IS NOT NULL AS deleted
FROM follows f JOIN subj USING (subject_did)
WHERE f.seen_at >= %(s)s AND f.seen_at < %(e)s
ORDER BY f.uri, f.seen_at
"""

_BACKGROUND_SQL = """
SELECT floor(extract(epoch FROM seen_at) - %(s_epoch)s)::int AS sec, count(*)
FROM {table} WHERE seen_at >= %(s)s AND seen_at < %(e)s GROUP BY 1
"""


def load_window(
    conn: psycopg.Connection, start: datetime, end: datetime, cfg: DetectorConfig
) -> WindowData:
    p = {

"""Detector entry point: window data -> scored clusters. Pure: no DB writes, deterministic.

    from signals.detect import detect
    results = detect(window_data, account_info=lambda dids: {...}, cfg=DEFAULT)

`account_info` is called once with all candidate members and returns {did: AccountInfo} for the
ones it knows (identity family and organic guards need it; pass None to skip them).
"""

import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from signals.config import DEFAULT, DetectorConfig
from signals.graph import build_graph, communities
from signals.keys import MinHashCache, build_keys
from signals.score import AccountInfo, ClusterScore, score_cluster
from signals.window import WindowData

AccountInfoFn = Callable[[list[str]], dict[str, AccountInfo]]


@dataclass
class DetectResult:
    clusters: list[ClusterScore]
    stats: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def detect(
    wd: WindowData,
    account_info: AccountInfoFn | None = None,
    cfg: DetectorConfig = DEFAULT,
    mh_cache: MinHashCache | None = None,
) -> DetectResult:
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    keys = build_keys(wd, cfg, mh_cache)
    t1 = time.monotonic()
    graph = build_graph(keys, cfg)
    groups = communities(graph, cfg)
    t2 = time.monotonic()
    # Pass 1 without account info. Then fetch account info only for clusters where something
    # looked suspicious (strongest first: the enrichment budget is limited) and rescore those.
    clusters = [score_cluster(g, keys, wd, {}, cfg) for g in groups]
    suspicious = sorted(
        (i for i, c in enumerate(clusters) if max(c.family_scores.values()) >= cfg.family_fire),
        key=lambda i: (-clusters[i].score, len(clusters[i].members), clusters[i].members[0]),
    )
    ordered = list(dict.fromkeys(d for i in suspicious for d in clusters[i].members))
    info = account_info(ordered) if account_info and ordered else {}
    t3 = time.monotonic()
    for i in suspicious:
        if any(d in info for d in clusters[i].members):
            clusters[i] = score_cluster(groups[i], keys, wd, info, cfg)
    t4 = time.monotonic()
    by_status: dict[str, int] = {}
    for c in clusters:
        by_status[c.status] = by_status.get(c.status, 0) + 1
    stats = {
        "posts": len(wd.posts),
        "actions": len(wd.actions),
        "keys": len(keys),
        "graph_accounts": len(graph.dids),
        "edges": len(graph.edges),
        "clusters": len(clusters),
        "by_status": by_status,
        "accounts_with_info": len(info),
        "seconds": {
            "keys": round(t1 - t0, 2),
            "graph": round(t2 - t1, 2),
            "score_and_enrich": round(t3 - t2, 2),
            "rescore": round(t4 - t3, 2),
        },
    }
    return DetectResult(clusters, stats)

    # empirical background used by the timing null model. kind -> array of len(end - start).
    background: dict[str, np.ndarray] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # Distinct accounts per kind over the whole stream in the window (for popularity / base rates).
    active_accounts: int = 0

    def background_for(self, kind: str) -> np.ndarray:
        bg = self.background.get(kind)
        n = max(1, int(round(self.end - self.start)))
        if bg is None or len(bg) == 0 or bg.sum() == 0:
            return np.ones(n)
        return bg

    @staticmethod
    def background_from_times(start: float, end: float, times_by_kind: dict[str, list[float]]):
        n = max(1, int(round(end - start)))
        out = {}
        for kind, times in times_by_kind.items():
            idx = np.clip((np.asarray(times, dtype=float) - start).astype(int), 0, n - 1)
            out[kind] = np.bincount(idx, minlength=n).astype(float)
        return out

       extract(epoch FROM created_at)::float8 AS created_t, deleted_at IS NOT NULL AS deleted, langs

       a.subject_uri, a.subject_did, a.deleted_at IS NOT NULL AS deleted

"""Account enrichment for cluster candidates only (never the whole stream).

- AppView app.bsky.actor.getProfiles (public.api.bsky.app, <= 25 actors per call): handle, display
  name, profile createdAt, follower/follow/post counts, avatar, bio length.
- PLC audit log (plc.directory/<did>/log/audit): DID creation time (first operation), number of
  handle changes, PDS host. did:web accounts have no PLC log.
Results are cached in `accounts` (profile_fetched_at / plc_fetched_at) and refreshed after a TTL.
"""

import logging
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import httpx
import psycopg

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

APPVIEW = "https://public.api.bsky.app/xrpc/app.bsky.actor.getProfiles"
PLC = "https://plc.directory"
PROFILE_TTL_H = 6
UA = {"User-Agent": "noise-radar-research/0.1 (read-only)"}


def _ts(s: str | None) -> datetime | None:
    if not s:

def normalize(event: dict) -> Row | None:
    """One Jetstream event -> one row, or None for events we don't store."""
    did = event.get("did")
    time_us = event.get("time_us")
    if not isinstance(did, str) or not isinstance(time_us, int):
        return None
    seen_at = us_to_dt(time_us)
    kind = event.get("kind")

    if kind == "account":
        acc = event.get("account") or {}
        return AccountEvent(
            did=did,
            kind="account",
            active=acc.get("active") if isinstance(acc.get("active"), bool) else None,
            status=clean(acc.get("status")) or ("active" if acc.get("active") else None),
            handle=None,
            seq=acc.get("seq") if isinstance(acc.get("seq"), int) else None,
            time_us=time_us,
            event_time=parse_ts(acc.get("time")),
        )
    if kind == "identity":
        ident = event.get("identity") or {}
        return AccountEvent(
            did=did,
            kind="identity",
            active=None,
            status=None,
            handle=clean(ident.get("handle")),
            seq=ident.get("seq") if isinstance(ident.get("seq"), int) else None,
            time_us=time_us,
            event_time=parse_ts(ident.get("time")),
        )
    if kind != "commit":
        return None

    commit = event.get("commit") or {}
    collection = commit.get("collection")
    rkey = commit.get("rkey")
    op = commit.get("operation")
    if collection not in TABLE_FOR or not isinstance(rkey, str):
        return None
    uri = f"at://{did}/{collection}/{rkey}"
    table = TABLE_FOR[collection]

    if op == "delete":
        return Delete(table=table, uri=uri, did=did, seen_at=seen_at)
    if op != "create":  # updates are rare for these collections; ignore them
        return None
    record = commit.get("record")
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        return None
    created_at = parse_ts(record.get("createdAt"))

    if collection == POST:
        text = clean(record.get("text"))
        langs = [clean(x) for x in record.get("langs") or [] if isinstance(x, str)][:5] or None
        post = Post(
            uri=uri,
            cid=clean(commit.get("cid")),
            did=did,
            text=text,
            langs=langs,
            created_at=created_at,
            seen_at=seen_at,
            text_hash=text_hash(text),
        )
        reply = record.get("reply")
        if isinstance(reply, dict):
            post.reply_to = _strong_ref_uri(reply.get("parent"))
            post.reply_root = _strong_ref_uri(reply.get("root"))
        _embed(record, post)
        _facets(record, post)
        return post

    if collection == FOLLOW:
        subject = clean(record.get("subject"))
        if not subject:
            return None
        return Action(table, uri, did, None, subject, created_at, seen_at)

    subject_uri = _strong_ref_uri(record.get("subject"))
    if not subject_uri:
        return None
    return Action(table, uri, did, subject_uri, did_of(subject_uri), created_at, seen_at)

            did=did,

            created_at=created_at,
            seen_at=seen_at,

        if not subject:

Each fixture will record the window start, case type, key, account and post counts, stats, and up to five sample accounts.

I'm settling on how to save the fixture: up to five sample post URIs or DIDs per case, with the key kept so the selection can be reproduced, and a note on why each case qualifies. I'm also considering whether committing these public identifiers to the repo is fine, and I'm thinking it is, since that's what the task asks for. Last, I'm setting the profile cache location under SLICES/accounts.

Now I'm settling how the profile and PLC data feed the age check: the account's birth date is the earlier of its PLC creation and its profile creation, and age is measured from the window end. For selection I only need the profile's creation date, and I'd fetch PLC for a DID only when that date is missing. I'm also sketching the synthetic runs, with a seed tied to the window, the attack kind, and the seed index.

I'm writing the evaluation function, which takes the clusters and the case's accounts and returns an outcome with hit details. Synthetic cases use the account set the generator supplies directly. Before settling on seeds, I'm checking whether the existing tests already use any, so the held-out seeds don't overlap with them.

I'm planning how the worker processes will handle account lookups, since the profile cache can't be written to safely from several processes at once. My leaning is to let each worker fetch what it's missing and return those results, then have the parent merge them into the cache afterward. The open question is that several workers may fetch the same DIDs at the same time, which wastes requests.

I'm going to run the four synthetic kinds with a few seeds per window, which comes to roughly 53 minutes serially and about 14 with four workers in parallel. # ------------------------------------------------------------------ split ---------------------
def split_of(window_start: float) -> str:
    """Held-out rule: a window belongs to the UTC hour it starts in; odd hours are `heldout`,
    even hours are `dev` (tuning). Whole hours, so neighbouring windows of one burst stay on
    one side."""
    return "heldout" if datetime.fromtimestamp(window_start, UTC).hour % 2 else "dev"


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ windows from recordings ---
@dataclass
class HourData:
    """Normalised rows of one recorded slice, bucketed into clock-aligned 10m windows."""

    posts: dict[int, dict[str, WPost]] = field(default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(dict))
    # window -> table -> uri -> (did, t, subject, subject_did)
    actions: dict[int, dict[str, dict[str, tuple]]] = field(
        default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(dict))
    )
    tags: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # post uri -> hashtags
    deletes: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)  # uri -> first delete time
    seconds: dict[int, set[int]] = field(default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(set))

    def complete_windows(self, min_covered: float = 0.98) -> list[int]:
        """Windows the recording covers: at least 98% of their seconds have events (the stream
        is hundreds of events/s, so an empty second means a gap, e.g. a recorder restart)."""
        return sorted(
            w for w, secs in self.seconds.items() if len(secs) >= min_covered * WINDOW_S
        )


def read_rows(paths: Iterable[Path]) -> HourData:
    data = HourData()
    for _raw, event in read_events(list(paths)):
        row = normalize(event)
        if row is None:
            continue
        if not isinstance(row, Post | Action | Delete):
            continue
        t = row.seen_at.timestamp()
        if isinstance(row, Delete):
            data.deletes.setdefault(row.uri, t)
            continue
        w = int(t // WINDOW_S) * WINDOW_S
        data.seconds[w].add(int(t))
        if isinstance(row, Post):
            if row.uri not in data.posts[w]:
                data.posts[w][row.uri] = WPost(
                    uri=row.uri,
                    did=row.did,
                    t=t,
                    text=row.text,
                    text_hash=row.text_hash,
                    embed_urls=row.embed_urls,
                    media_hashes=row.media_hashes,
                    reply_to=row.reply_to,
                    reply_root=row.reply_root,
                    quote_uri=row.quote_uri,
                    created_t=row.created_at.timestamp() if row.created_at else None,
                    langs=row.langs or [],
                )
                if row.tags:
                    data.tags[row.uri] = row.tags
        else:
            subject = row.subject_uri if row.table != "follows" else row.subject_did
            data.actions[w][row.table].setdefault(row.uri, (row.did, t, subject, row.subject_did))
    return data

Next I'm moving on to the runner and the CLI, and I'm planning a run_hour function that takes the paths, split, profiles, seeds, cases, config, and worker count, then returns the case results and window metadata. """The one writer for `eval_runs` (db/schema.sql). `/api/metrics` serves the latest row per
(dataset, split), and the dashboard shows it, so every number there comes from a row this wrote."""

import json

import psycopg


def write_eval_run(
    dataset: str,
    split: str,
    *,
    n: int,
    details: dict,
    precision: float | None = None,
    recall: float | None = None,
    f1: float | None = None,
    fpr: float | None = None,
    database_url: str | None = None,
    conn: psycopg.Connection | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Insert one eval run and return its id. Pass an open `conn`, or a `database_url`
    (default: DATABASE_URL from the environment / .env)."""
    sql = """
        INSERT INTO eval_runs (dataset, split, precision, recall, f1, fpr, n, details)
        VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb) RETURNING id
    """
    args = (dataset, split, precision, recall, f1, fpr, n, json.dumps(details))
    if conn is not None:
        return conn.execute(sql, args).fetchone()[0]
    if database_url is None:
        from common.config import get_settings

        database_url = get_settings().database_url
    with psycopg.connect(database_url, connect_timeout=5) as c:
        rid = c.execute(sql, args).fetchone()[0]
        c.commit()
        return rid

"""The one writer for `eval_runs` (db/schema.sql). `/api/metrics` serves the latest row per
(dataset, split), and the dashboard shows it, so every number there comes from a row this wrote."""

import json

import psycopg


def write_eval_run(
    dataset: str,
    split: str,
    *,
    n: int,
    details: dict,
    precision: float | None = None,
    recall: float | None = None,
    f1: float | None = None,
    fpr: float | None = None,
    database_url: str | None = None,
    conn: psycopg.Connection | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Insert one eval run and return its id. Pass an open `conn`, or a `database_url`
    (default: DATABASE_URL from the environment / .env)."""
    sql = """
        INSERT INTO eval_runs (dataset, split, precision, recall, f1, fpr, n, details)
        VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb) RETURNING id
    """
    args = (dataset, split, precision, recall, f1, fpr, n, json.dumps(details))
    if conn is not None:

    if database_url is None:
        from common.config import get_settings

        database_url = get_settings().database_url
    with psycopg.connect(database_url, connect_timeout=5) as c:
        rid = c.execute(sql, args).fetchone()[0]
        c.commit()
        return rid

I'm noticing that normalize_url isn't stripping the ?CMP=Share_iOSApp_Other tracking parameter, which looks like Kirill's normalizer behaving as it does, likely a fragmentation issue rather than a false positive, worth mentioning in the PR. I also think the link threshold of 8 is too high for a 10-minute window, since the top link only reaches 7 accounts, so I'm considering lowering link_min_accounts to 5 to catch breaking-news links like the Guardian at 7 and The Hill at 6.

I'm checking the nextstamina.com accounts, three each, which looks like a bot network, and I think the existing filter would already catch it. The hashtags "srbger" and "lastfourwatched" look fine, one a live match and one a meme game. I'm also weighing whether the popular-post outcome is too loose: with 643 engagers, two of them could easily sit in an unrelated coordinated cluster, so I'm considering requiring a larger share of the cluster's members to overlap.

I'm weighing whether to require that the cluster be mostly made up of this case's accounts, at least half its members, so a stray overlap of two doesn't count as a false positive for an unrelated cluster.

I'm setting the min-share requirement to 0.5 so a cluster only counts when most of its members are this case's accounts. Next I'll run a smoke eval with one window and one seed.

The link threshold is being lowered from 8 to 5, since the max seen in 10-minute windows is 7. I'm also requiring a cluster to have at least 2 members and at least half of them be case accounts before it counts toward a case.

"""Organic false-positive eval: window building from recordings, the live-case selection rule,
case scoring and the summary. Offline: no network, no database."""

import gzip
import json
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from eval import organic
from eval.organic import (
    LIVE_RULE,
    WINDOW_S,
    CaseResult,
    HourData,
    Profiles,
    account_info_fn,
    build_window,
    candidate_keys,
    case_outcome,
    read_rows,
    select_live_cases,
    split_of,
    summarize,
)
from eval.store import write_eval_run
from signals.synth import empty_window, hard_negative
from signals.window import WPost

W = 1_794_600_000  # 2026-11-13T20:40:00Z, a clock-aligned 10-minute window
AT = W + WINDOW_S
OLD = datetime.fromtimestamp(W - 800 * 86400, UTC).isoformat()
NEW = datetime.fromtimestamp(W - 5 * 86400, UTC).isoformat()


def _profiles(n: int, created: str = OLD, followers: int = 200, posts: int = 500) -> Profiles:
    p = Profiles(None, fetch=False)
    for i in range(n):
        p.data[f"did:plc:u{i}"] = {
            "handle": f"u{i}.bsky.social",
            "created": created,
            "followers": followers,
            "posts": posts,
            "plc": None,
        }
    return p


def _post(i: int, t: float, text: str, urls=(), uri_n: int = 0) -> WPost:
    return WPost(
        uri=f"at://did:plc:u{i}/app.bsky.feed.post/p{uri_n}",
        did=f"did:plc:u{i}",
        t=t,
        text=text,
        embed_urls=list(urls),
    )


def _hour(posts: list[WPost], tags: dict | None = None) -> HourData:
    d = HourData()
    for p in posts:
        d.posts[W][p.uri] = p
    d.tags.update(tags or {})
    return d


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ split / windows -----------
def test_split_is_by_utc_hour_parity():
    assert split_of(datetime(2026, 11, 13, 19, 50, tzinfo=UTC).timestamp()) == "heldout"
    assert split_of(datetime(2026, 11, 13, 20, 0, tzinfo=UTC).timestamp()) == "dev"
    assert split_of(datetime(2026, 11, 13, 21, 59, tzinfo=UTC).timestamp()) == "heldout"


def _event(did, t, collection, rkey, record=None, op="create"):
    commit = {"operation": op, "collection": collection, "rkey": rkey}
    if record is not None:
        commit["record"] = record
    return {"did": did, "time_us": int(t * 1e6), "kind": "commit", "commit": commit}


def test_window_from_recording_mirrors_load_window(tmp_path):
    like = "app.bsky.feed.like"
    subj = lambda k: {"subject": {"uri": f"at://did:plc:author/app.bsky.feed.post/{k}"}}  # noqa: E731
    events = []
    # one event per second so the window counts as fully recorded
    for s in range(WINDOW_S):
        events.append(_event(f"did:plc:bg{s}", W + s + 0.5, like, f"b{s}", subj(f"solo{s}")))
    # a subject liked by 3 accounts (kept), one liked by 1 account (dropped: < min_key_accounts)
    for i in range(3):
        events.append(_event(f"did:plc:l{i}", W + 10 + i, like, "x", subj("shared")))
    post = {"text": "hello world from a recorded slice #Tag", "createdAt": "2026-11-13T20:40:05Z"}
    post["facets"] = [{"features": [{"$type": "app.bsky.richtext.facet#tag", "tag": "Tag"}]}]
    events.append(_event("did:plc:p", W + 5, "app.bsky.feed.post", "a", post))
    events.append(_event("did:plc:p", W + 6, "app.bsky.feed.post", "a", post))  # duplicate
    events.append(_event("did:plc:p", W + 7, "app.bsky.feed.post", "b", post))
    events.append(_event("did:plc:p", W + 8, "app.bsky.feed.post", "b", op="delete"))
    events.append(_event("did:plc:p", W + 9, "app.bsky.feed.post", "a", op="delete"))
    events[-1]["time_us"] = int((AT + 30) * 1e6)  # deleted only after the window ended
    path = tmp_path / "20261113" / "20-1.jsonl.gz"
    path.parent.mkdir()
    with gzip.open(path, "wt") as fh:
        for e in events:
            fh.write(json.dumps(e) + "\n")

    data = read_rows([path])
    assert data.complete_windows() == [W]
    assert data.tags["at://did:plc:p/app.bsky.feed.post/a"] == ["tag"]
    wd = build_window(data, W)
    assert [p.uri.rsplit("/", 1)[1] for p in wd.posts] == ["a", "b"]
    assert [p.deleted for p in wd.posts] == [False, True]
    assert {a.subject.rsplit("/", 1)[1] for a in wd.actions} == {"shared"}
    assert len(wd.actions) == 3
    assert wd.background["like"].sum() == WINDOW_S + 3
    assert wd.background["post"].sum() == 2
    assert wd.active_accounts == 1


def test_partial_window_is_not_complete():
    d = HourData()
    d.seconds[W] = set(range(W, W + 300))
    assert d.complete_windows() == []


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ live-case rule -----------
LINK = "https://news.example/2026/11/13/story"


def test_link_shared_by_established_accounts_with_own_words_is_selected():
    posts = [_post(i, W + 30 * i, f"my own take number {i} on this {i * 7}", [LINK]) for i in range(6)]
    cases = select_live_cases(_hour(posts), W, _profiles(6))
    assert [c["type"] for c in cases] == ["link_burst"]
    c = cases[0]
    assert c["key"] == LINK and c["accounts"] == 6 and c["established_share"] == 1.0
    assert c["split"] == "dev" and c["sample_urls"][0].startswith("https://bsky.app/profile/")
    assert "6 accounts posted the same link" in c["why"]


def test_copy_paste_text_is_not_an_organic_case():
    posts = [_post(i, W + i, "exact same words from everyone here", [LINK]) for i in range(6)]
    assert candidate_keys(_hour(posts), W) == []


def test_too_few_accounts_or_one_account_repeating_is_rejected():
    few = [_post(i, W + i, f"take {i} different", [LINK]) for i in range(LIVE_RULE["link_min_accounts"] - 1)]
    assert candidate_keys(_hour(few), W) == []
    spam = [_post(i, W + i, f"take {i} different", [LINK]) for i in range(6)]
    spam += [_post(0, W + 100 + k, f"again {k} and again", [LINK], uri_n=k + 1) for k in range(4)]
    assert candidate_keys(_hour(spam), W) == []


def test_fresh_or_unknown_accounts_are_not_established():
    posts = [_post(i, W + i, f"my own take number {i}", [LINK]) for i in range(6)]
    assert select_live_cases(_hour(posts), W, _profiles(6, created=NEW)) == []
    assert select_live_cases(_hour(posts), W, _profiles(6, followers=3)) == []
    assert select_live_cases(_hour(posts), W, Profiles(None, fetch=False)) == []


def test_hashtag_burst_and_popular_post():
    posts = [_post(i, W + i, f"what a match {i} wow {i * 3}") for i in range(8)]
    tags = {p.uri: ["final"] for p in posts}
    data = _hour(posts, tags)
    subject = "at://did:plc:star/app.bsky.feed.post/1"
    n = LIVE_RULE["post_min_engagers"]
    for i in range(n):
        data.actions[W]["likes"][f"at://did:plc:u{i}/app.bsky.feed.like/1"] = (
            f"did:plc:u{i}",
            W + i,
            subject,
            "did:plc:star",
        )
    cases = select_live_cases(data, W, _profiles(n))
    assert {(c["type"], c["key"]) for c in cases} == {
        ("hashtag_burst", "final"),
        ("popular_post", subject),
    }
    accounts, _ = organic.case_accounts(data, W, "popular_post", subject)
    assert len(accounts) == n


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ scoring ------------------
def _cluster(status, members, fired=("content", "timing")):
    sig = SimpleNamespace(name="duplicate_text", polarity="for", score=1.0)
    guard = SimpleNamespace(name="established_accounts", polarity="against", score=0.7)
    return SimpleNamespace(
        status=status,
        members=list(members),
        score=0.9,
        p_value=0.002,
        guard_score=0.1,
        families_fired=list(fired),
        signals=[sig, guard],
    )


def test_case_outcome_takes_the_worst_status_of_clusters_about_the_case():
    case = {f"c{i}" for i in range(10)}
    org = _cluster("likely_organic", ["c0", "c1", "c2"])
    assert case_outcome([org], case)[0] == "likely_organic"
    coord = _cluster("coordinated", ["c3", "c4", "x1"])
    outcome, hits = case_outcome([org, coord], case)
    assert outcome == "coordinated"
    assert hits[0]["status"] == "coordinated" and hits[0]["overlap"] == 2
    assert hits[0]["signals_for"] == ["duplicate_text"]
    assert hits[0]["guards"] == ["established_accounts"]
    assert case_outcome([_cluster("insufficient", ["c5", "c6"])], case)[0] == "insufficient"
    assert case_outcome([], case)[0] == "no_cluster"


def test_case_outcome_ignores_clusters_that_are_not_about_the_case():
    case = {f"c{i}" for i in range(10)}
    one = _cluster("coordinated", ["c0", "x1", "x2"])  # only 1 case account
    minority = _cluster("coordinated", ["c0", "c1"] + [f"x{i}" for i in range(8)])  # 20%
    assert case_outcome([one, minority], case)[0] == "no_cluster"


def test_summary_counts_fpr_and_lists_false_positives():
    _, hits = case_outcome([_cluster("coordinated", ["a", "b"])], {"a", "b"})
    rs = [
        CaseResult("fp1", "organic_live", "link_burst", W, 2, "coordinated", hits),
        CaseResult("ok1", "organic_live", "link_burst", W, 5, "likely_organic"),
        CaseResult("ok2", "organic_live", "hashtag_burst", W, 9, "insufficient"),
        CaseResult("ok3", "organic_live", "hashtag_burst", W, 9, "no_cluster"),
    ]
    s = summarize(rs)
    assert s["n"] == 4 and s["fpr"] == 0.25
    assert s["counts"] == {"coordinated": 1, "likely_organic": 1, "insufficient": 1, "no_cluster": 1}
    assert s["clustered"] == 3 and s["fpr_given_clustered"] == pytest.approx(0.3333)
    assert s["by_type"]["link_burst"] == {
        "n": 2,
        "coordinated": 1,
        "likely_organic": 1,
        "insufficient": 0,
        "no_cluster": 0,
        "fpr": 0.5,
    }
    assert s["false_positives"][0]["case_id"] == "fp1"
    assert s["false_positives"][0]["families_fired"] == ["content", "timing"]
    lo, hi = s["fpr_ci95"]
    assert 0 < lo < 0.25 < hi < 1
    assert summarize([])["fpr"] is None


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ detector glue ------------
def test_account_info_budget_and_synthetic_accounts():
    p = _profiles(5)
    s = hard_negative("news_link", empty_window(), seed=1)
    synth = sorted(s.dids)[:2]
    fn = account_info_fn(p, AT, s, budget=3)
    out = fn(synth + [f"did:plc:u{i}" for i in range(5)])
    assert set(out) == set(synth) | {"did:plc:u0", "did:plc:u1", "did:plc:u2"}
    assert out["did:plc:u0"].age_days == pytest.approx(800)


def test_synthetic_hard_negatives_on_a_synthetic_background_are_not_coordinated():
    """End to end through the detector's entry point (no recording needed)."""
    from signals.detect import detect
    from signals.synth import inject

    base = empty_window(start=W, seed=11)
    for kind in ("news_link", "live_event", "fandom"):
        s = hard_negative(kind, base, seed=1000)
        res = detect(inject(base, s), account_info_fn(Profiles(None, fetch=False), AT, s))
        assert case_outcome(res.clusters, s.dids)[0] != "coordinated", kind


def test_write_eval_run_inserts_one_row():
    calls = []

    class Conn:
        def execute(self, sql, args):
            calls.append((sql, args))
            return SimpleNamespace(fetchone=lambda: (42,))

    rid = write_eval_run("organic_live", "heldout", n=19, fpr=0.0, details={"a": 1}, conn=Conn())
    assert rid == 42
    sql, args = calls[0]
    assert "INSERT INTO eval_runs" in sql
    assert args == ("organic_live", "heldout", None, None, None, 0.0, 19, '{"a": 1}')

# eval/: measured error rates

Every metric on the dashboard is a row in `eval_runs` (`db/schema.sql`) written by this package
(`eval/store.py`, the one writer). `/api/metrics` serves the latest row per `(dataset, split)`.

```bash
uv run python -m eval organic select   # pick live organic cases -> eval/fixtures/organic_live.json
uv run python -m eval organic run      # run the detector, print the report, write nothing
uv run python -m eval organic run --write --database-url postgresql://...   # -> eval_runs
uv run pytest tests/test_eval_organic.py
```

## Data and the held-out split

- Recordings: raw Jetstream files from `ingest --record` (`/srv/junction-espoo/data/jetstream`,
  pruned after 24 h). Slices we keep are copied to `/srv/junction-espoo/data/eval-slices/jetstream/`
  (same `YYYYMMDD/HH-<start>.jsonl.gz` layout; override with `EVAL_SLICES_DIR`).
- Windows: clock-aligned 10-minute windows (the detector's main window). A window is used only if
  at least 98% of its seconds have events (no recorder gaps).
- **Split by UTC hour: a window belongs to the hour it starts in; odd hours are `heldout`, even
  hours are `dev`.** Tune on `dev`, report `heldout`. Whole hours keep the windows of one burst
  on one side.
- No database: windows are built in memory from the recordings with the ingest normaliser
  (`ingest.normalize`), making the same selection as `signals.window.load_window`, then scored
  with the detector's own entry point `signals.detect.detect`. Detector code is never copied or
  changed here. One difference from live: `deleted` only counts deletes seen before the window
  ends.
- Account info: public AppView profiles and PLC logs via `signals.enrich`'s read-only fetchers,
  cached in `eval-slices/accounts/profiles.json` so re-runs see the same numbers. Like production,
  only the first 400 accounts of the detector's priority list are enriched per pass (`--budget`).

## Organic false positives (`organic_synth`, `organic_live`)

Hostinger's judges weigh how we handle false positives above everything else. This measures how
often the detector calls organic activity `coordinated` (🚩 Shill).

| dataset | cases | labels |
|---|---|---|
| `organic_synth` | `signals.synth.hard_negative` kinds `viral`, `news_link`, `live_event`, `fandom`, injected one at a time into every held-out window, seeds 1000+ (Kirill's tests use seed 0; `dev` uses 0+) | synthetic, true by construction |
| `organic_live` | real bursts in the held-out recordings, picked by the rule below, listed in `eval/fixtures/organic_live.json` | **heuristic, not ground truth** until a human checks a sample |

**Live-case rule (`live-rule-v1`, never reads detector output).** In each complete window:
(a) a normalised link posted by >= 5 distinct accounts, or (b) a hashtag used by >= 8 distinct
accounts, where no account posts it more than 3 times and <= 20% of the posts reuse another
account's normalised text; or (c) one of the 10 posts liked/reposted by the most (>= 50) distinct
accounts. Then a deterministic sample of up to 40 of its accounts is looked up: >= 80% must
resolve, and >= 80% of those must be >= 365 days old with >= 30 followers and >= 30 posts.
Thresholds live in `LIVE_RULE` and are copied into the fixture.

Caveat: "established accounts" is also an input to the detector's `established_accounts` guard
(> 365 days, >= 100 followers), so the live set leans towards cases that guard can see. The
synthetic set and the per-type breakdown are there to show the rest.

**Outcome per case**: the worst status among clusters where the case's accounts are >= 2 members
and >= 50% of the cluster: `coordinated` (a false positive) > `likely_organic` (😎 Chill) >
`insufficient` (🤷 abstained) > `no_cluster` (never grouped, so never shown).

**Row**: `fpr` = coordinated / n, `n` = cases; precision/recall/F1 are empty (no positives).
`details` has `counts` per outcome, `fpr_ci95` (Wilson), `clustered` and `fpr_given_clustered`
(the harder number: no_cluster cases are easy wins), `by_type`, `false_positives` (case id, the
clusters and which signal families fired: the error analysis), `detector_version`, `eval_code`
(git sha), windows, slice files, seeds or fixture.

# claude-code review

**Verdict: request changes.** The eval's numbers depend on cache state, worker scheduling and job order, and transient fetch failures are cached permanently. That undercuts the README's promises that re-runs see the same numbers and that enrichment matches production.

I could not run the tests: `uv run pytest` needed permission, which this session didn't get. The findings come from reading the source.

- [high] eval/organic.py:320 — Because the budget now only limits fetching, a pass sees everything the shared `Profiles` cache has gathered so far, and that changes with job order. Each window runs about 13 detector passes (the live pass, then 4 kinds × 3 seeds) and each can fetch another 400 accounts. With `--workers 1`, the last fandom seed can therefore see up to about 5200 enriched real accounts, where production sees 400. With workers > 1, which accounts a job sees depends on which forked worker ran it and what that worker ran before, since the copies only merge at the end of the hour. A cold-cache run also differs from a warm one. So the same split gives different FPRs across runs and worker counts, which contradicts README "re-runs see the same numbers". Fix: give each pass a fixed view, for example a snapshot of the cache taken before the hour plus only that pass's own budgeted fetches, or pre-enrich once per window with the live pass's priority list and keep it frozen for all passes.

- [medium] eval/organic.py:250 — `fetch_profiles` skips any 25-account chunk whose HTTP request fails or returns non-200 (signals/enrich.py:56). `ensure` then caches each of those accounts as `{"missing": True}`, and the PLC result as `None`, for good. `needs()` never retries them and `info()` returns `None`. One rate-limited or timed-out request (more likely now that several workers fetch the same accounts) permanently makes real accounts look unresolved. That lowers `resolved_share` in `select` and removes them from detector info in later runs. Fix: cache `missing` only for a successful 200 response that leaves the DID out, and don't cache transport or non-200 failures, or give them a retry TTL.

- [medium] eval/organic.py:276 — `info()` returns `None` when the profile is missing and PLC failed. Production `load_account_info` returns an `AccountInfo` with null fields for any account it has tried to fetch (signals/enrich.py:126 always sets `profile_fetched_at`). The detector counts `known = [info[d] ... if d in info]` (signals/score.py:445) and only rescores when `any(d in info ...)` (signals/detect.py:52). So clusters of deleted or suspended accounts score differently in the eval than in production. Fix: return a null-field `AccountInfo` for every entry that was attempted, to match `load_account_info`.

- [medium] eval/organic.py:411 — The duplicate-text check normalises empty or None text to `""`, and every empty-text post then counts as reusing another account's text. Link-card posts with no text from 2+ accounts can push `duplicate_text_share` over 0.2 and reject a real organic link burst. This skews which live cases are selected. Fix: leave out empty normalised text (or text below a minimum length) when computing `dup`.

- [medium] eval/organic.py:684 — Each forked worker has its own copy of `Profiles` and fetches separately, so the same top-priority accounts of a window get fetched up to `workers` times against the public AppView and PLC. That wastes requests and makes rate limiting (and so the cached "missing" failures above) more likely. Fix: enrich each window once in the parent before dispatching jobs, then run the workers offline.

- [low] eval/organic.py:788 — In `select`, `--max-windows` is applied per hour (`complete_windows()[: a.max_windows]`). In `run`, `run_eval` (lines 663-670) applies it as a total. The same flag selects many more windows in `select` than `run` scores, so the fixture can hold cases that a capped `run` never evaluates. Fix: track a running total in `select` as `run_eval` does.

- [low] eval/organic.py:810 — When the fixture is missing, `run` falls back to `{"cases": []}` without a warning, and `eval/fixtures/organic_live.json` is not committed. A default run therefore reports `organic_live` with n=0 and `--write` skips it with only `skip ... n=0`. Separately, `select` (line 806) overwrites an existing, possibly human-reviewed fixture even when it found no slices. Fix: commit the fixture (or fail loudly when it is absent in `run`), and refuse to overwrite with 0 cases unless forced.

- [low] eval/organic.py:612 — `_job` rebuilds the same base window with `build_window(data, w, cfg)` for every job on that window (13× by default). For the viral injection, `inject` also copies the full post and action lists each time. Fix: build each window once per hour in the parent before forking, store it in `_G`, and reuse it in `_job`.

- [low] eval/organic.py:462 — `select_live_cases` calls `case_accounts` twice for every passing candidate (lines 448 and 462) and scans all window posts or actions each time. Fix: keep `uris` from the first call alongside the sample.

I'm weighing the determinism issue: the earlier fix made the info grow with the cache, so each pass sees a different view. My leaning is to enrich once in the parent per window, run the live base pass first to fill the cache up to budget, then hand the synthesis passes offline workers with a snapshot taken after that base pass. The open question is whether those passes' info still depends on the cache built during selection and earlier windows.

I'm still weighing how to keep each pass's view the same across runs, since a warm cache and a cold one produce different results. Tying the view to the per-window budget would be reproducible but drops the accumulated state that production really has. The open tension is between that conservative fixed view and a more realistic accumulating one.

I'm going back and forth on whether each pass should see a fixed, cold-cache view of the first `budget` accounts so evals stay reproducible, or an accumulating view that matches production's steady state. Sol's counterexample shows production would carry enriched accounts across minute passes, but a deterministic cold-pass view is easier to defend for reporting, so I'm leaning toward that and documenting it as a single cold detector pass.

I'm settling on a per-pass view that is the first `budget` accounts of the priority list, which makes results deterministic regardless of cache state. Across passes in a production window the view would accumulate, but within a single pass that cold view is what I'll document, since I'd mis-described the original design as mirroring production.

I'm settling on a per-pass view of the first `budget` accounts in the priority list, independent of cache state, because the determinism problem across worker counts is real and Sol's fix caused it. The tradeoff is that this is a single cold pass and less like production's accumulating state, so I'll document that plainly and still give synthesis passes their info from memory.

I'm settling on a cache-independent view for missing accounts, so a transient fetch failure doesn't get stored as "absent." The tricky part is that the fetch helper returns an empty result for failed chunks just like for genuinely missing accounts, so I can't tell them apart. My leaning is to simply not cache absent results at all, accepting a few repeat fetches for accounts that really don't exist.

Checking whether a failed fetch leaves a null-field AccountInfo behind, the way production does: enrich always sets profile_fetched_at, and load_account_info only skips rows where both fetched timestamps are null, so attempted accounts still come back with whatever the accounts table holds.

I'm working through the determinism problem: a per-pass view of the first `budget` accounts keeps results reproducible, though it loses the accumulated state production would carry across passes. For accounts whose fetch fails, I'll record a null-field entry for this run without caching the failure, so retries happen next time and repeat attempts within a run stay bounded. On the duplicate-text check, empty normalized posts shouldn't count toward duplicates.

I'm handling the duplicate-text check by leaving out empty posts, since they don't show whether accounts are writing their own words. If nothing non-empty remains, I'd reject rather than count it as diverse. I'm also weighing whether the base pass should run in the parent first so synthesis workers don't keep re-fetching the same top accounts.

The two-batch idea is the cleanest way to cut down repeat fetches: base passes run first and fill the cache, then the synthesis passes start from that warm cache. I'll also fix the --max-windows count with a running total, and add a check that fails loudly if the fixture is missing.

I'm making the profile lookup per pass deterministic: each pass works only from the first `budget` accounts, and any account we tried but couldn't load still gets a null-field entry for that run, matching how production keeps attempted accounts. I'm also tracking attempts in memory only, so failed fetches aren't saved and get retried on the next run.

I'm moving the profile cache toward attempted-but-failed accounts getting a null-field entry for the run, while keeping failures out of the saved file so they get retried next time. Old cache entries marked as missing or as failed PLC lookups are the open question, since they may have come from transient errors.

I'm reworking the profile cache so that failed lookups aren't saved as "missing," and the info helper will just return nothing for those. I also need to handle the case where a PLC lookup succeeds but the profile doesn't, so the stored entry doesn't break on a missing key.

I'm switching to a two-stage run: the base passes go first to warm the cache, then the synthesis passes. Since the per-pass view is fixed, the staging only saves fetches, so I'm rewriting the Profiles class so successes are the only things stored and failed attempts stay in memory for the run.

The review turned up several real problems, mostly from my round-1 fix: results weren't reproducible, failed fetches were cached forever, and duplicate fetches ran across workers. I'm fixing these now, starting with a fixed set of 400 accounts per pass and running live passes before synthetic ones.

    """Run every job on the complete windows of the requested split. Returns (results, per-pass
    detector stats, slice files used)."""
    from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
    from multiprocessing import get_context

    results: list[CaseResult] = []
    stats: list[dict] = []
    files: list[str] = []
    done = 0
    for hour, paths in slice_hours(slices).items():
        if hour_split(hour) != split or (max_windows is not None and done >= max_windows):
            continue
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        data = read_rows(paths)
        windows = data.complete_windows()
        if max_windows is not None:
            windows = windows[: max_windows - done]
        done += len(windows)
        if not windows:
            continue
        files += [str(p) for p in paths]
        log.info("hour %s: %d windows (read in %.0fs)", hour, len(windows), time.monotonic() - t0)
        _G.update(data=data, profiles=profiles, cfg=cfg, budget=budget)
        jobs = []
        for w in windows:
            ws = datetime.fromtimestamp(w, UTC).isoformat()
            live = [c for c in live_cases if c["window_start"] == ws]
            jobs.append((w, None, None, live))
            jobs += [(w, k, s, []) for k in kinds for s in seeds]
        if workers > 1:
            with ProcessPoolExecutor(workers, mp_context=get_context("fork")) as pool:
                outs = list(pool.map(_job, *zip(*jobs, strict=True)))
        else:
            outs = [_job(*j) for j in jobs]
        for rs, st, new in outs:
            results += rs
            stats.append(st)
            profiles.merge(new)
            profiles.fetched += len(new)
        profiles.save()
        _G.clear()
    return results, stats, files

Writes FPR + details to eval_runs via eval/store.py. An eval must be reproducible: same slices + same cache-independent inputs => same numbers regardless of job order / worker count.

"""The one writer for `eval_runs` (db/schema.sql). `/api/metrics` serves the latest row per
(dataset, split), and the dashboard shows it, so every number there comes from a row this wrote."""

import json

import psycopg


def write_eval_run(
    dataset: str,
    split: str,
    *,
    n: int,
    details: dict,
    precision: float | None = None,
    recall: float | None = None,
    f1: float | None = None,
    fpr: float | None = None,
    database_url: str | None = None,
    conn: psycopg.Connection | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Insert one eval run and return its id. Pass an open `conn`, or a `database_url`
    (default: DATABASE_URL from the environment / .env)."""
    sql = """
        INSERT INTO eval_runs (dataset, split, precision, recall, f1, fpr, n, details)
        VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb) RETURNING id
    """
    args = (dataset, split, precision, recall, f1, fpr, n, json.dumps(details))
    if conn is not None:
        return conn.execute(sql, args).fetchone()[0]
    if database_url is None:
        from common.config import get_settings

        database_url = get_settings().database_url
    with psycopg.connect(database_url, connect_timeout=5) as c:
        rid = c.execute(sql, args).fetchone()[0]
        c.commit()
        return rid
"""Eval CLI: `python -m eval <subcommand>`.

recall        recall on synthetic campaigns injected into recorded windows (eval/recall.py)
copy-slices   keep recorded Jetstream hours (the recorder prunes after 24 h) (eval/slices.py)
"""

import argparse
import logging
import sys

from eval import recall, slices


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m eval")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    recall.add_arguments(sub.add_parser("recall", help="recall on synthetic campaigns"))
    slices.add_arguments(sub.add_parser("copy-slices", help="copy recorded hours for eval"))
    a = p.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    if a.command == "recall":
        return recall.main_args(a)
    if a.command == "copy-slices":
        return slices.main_args(a)
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
"""Recorded Jetstream slices -> detector windows, in memory (no database).

The live recorder (`ingest --record`) keeps hourly gzip files for 24 h only, so the hours we
evaluate on are copied to SLICE_ROOT (shared, outside git). `iter_windows` reads them with the
ingest normaliser and builds the same `WindowData` that `signals.window.load_window` builds from
Postgres: posts in the window, likes/reposts/follows whose subject got 2..max_key_accounts
distinct accounts in the window, per-second background counts of every event, and the number of
distinct posting accounts.

Splits are whole UTC hours (odd = heldout, even = dev). Never tune anything on `heldout` hours.
"""

import argparse
import logging
import shutil
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from ingest.normalize import Action, Delete, Post, normalize
from ingest.recorder import read_events, recorded_files
from signals.config import DEFAULT, DetectorConfig
from signals.window import WAction, WindowData, WPost

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

RECORD_ROOT = Path("/srv/junction-espoo/data/jetstream")
SLICE_ROOT = Path("/srv/junction-espoo/data/eval-slices/jetstream")

# Split rule (shared by every eval in eval/): a window belongs to the UTC hour it starts in; odd
# hours are `heldout`, even hours are `dev`. Whole hours, so one burst never straddles splits.
SPLITS = ("dev", "heldout")


def split_of_hour(hour: str) -> str:
    """'2026111321' -> 'heldout' (odd UTC hour), '2026111320' -> 'dev'."""
    return "heldout" if int(hour[8:10]) % 2 else "dev"


MAX_GAP_S = 60.0  # a window with a longer hole in the recording is skipped, not evaluated
REORDER_S = 120.0  # events can arrive this much out of order (cursor rewind, host failover)


def file_hour(path: Path) -> str:
    """'<root>/20261113/19-1794598897.jsonl.gz' -> '2026111319'."""
    return f"{path.parent.name}{path.name[:2]}"


def hour_files(root: Path, hours: Iterable[str]) -> list[Path]:
    wanted = set(hours)
    return [p for p in recorded_files(root) if file_hour(p) in wanted]


def recorded_hours(root: Path) -> list[str]:
    return sorted({file_hour(p) for p in recorded_files(root)})


def split_hours(root: Path, split: str) -> list[str]:
    """Every recorded hour under root that belongs to this split."""
    return [h for h in recorded_hours(root) if split_of_hour(h) == split]


def copy_hours(src: Path, dst: Path, hours: Iterable[str]) -> list[Path]:
    """Copy the recorded files of these hours from src to dst (same layout). Existing files of the
    same name are overwritten only if the source is bigger (the hour was still being written)."""
    out = []
    for p in hour_files(src, hours):
        target = dst / p.parent.name / p.name
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not target.exists() or target.stat().st_size < p.stat().st_size:
            shutil.copy2(p, target)
        out.append(target)
    return out


@dataclass
class _Bucket:
    """Raw events of one window, before the load_window-equivalent filtering."""

    posts: dict[str, WPost] = field(default_factory=dict)
    actions: dict[str, list[tuple]] = field(
        default_factory=lambda: {"like": [], "repost": [], "follow": []}
    )
    deletes: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    times: dict[str, list[float]] = field(
        default_factory=lambda: {"post": [], "like": [], "repost": [], "follow": []}
    )
    ticks: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)  # every event time, to find holes

    def coverage(self) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
        """(first, last, longest gap) over the window's events, in time order (events can
        arrive out of order, so gaps are measured after sorting)."""
        t = np.sort(np.asarray(self.ticks))
        gap = float(np.diff(t).max()) if len(t) > 1 else 0.0
        return float(t[0]), float(t[-1]), gap


_KIND = {"likes": "like", "reposts": "repost", "follows": "follow"}


def _to_window(b: _Bucket, start: float, end: float, cfg: DetectorConfig) -> WindowData:
    wd = WindowData(start=start, end=end)
    for uri in sorted(b.posts):
        p = b.posts[uri]
        p.deleted = uri in b.deletes
        wd.posts.append(p)
    lo, hi = cfg.min_key_accounts, cfg.max_key_accounts
    for kind in ("like", "repost", "follow"):
        rows = b.actions[kind]
        # (uri, did, t, subject_uri_or_did, subject_did); key = subject_uri, or subject_did (follow)
        by_subject: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
        for r in rows:
            by_subject[r[3]].add(r[1])
        keep = {s for s, dids in by_subject.items() if lo <= len(dids) <= hi}
        for r in sorted((r for r in rows if r[3] in keep), key=lambda r: r[0]):

content.text:
It isn't idle waiting. The detector is doing the work, and the server is overloaded:

- **The work:** the held-out set is 7 ten-minute windows. Each window needs 13 full detector passes (1 for the live cases, plus 4 synthetic kinds × 3 seeds), so 91 passes in total. One pass on a real window takes about 35 s unloaded: keys, a 500-permutation null model, then profile/PLC lookups for up to 400 accounts. With 4 workers that should be about 12–15 min.
- **The slowdown:** load average is **27 on 8 cores**. Other threads (the recall eval, calibration and so on) are running detector jobs at the same time, so each pass runs about 3× slower.
- **Progress:** hour 19 (1 window) is done. Hour 21 (6 windows, 78 passes) has been running for 18 min. At this load I expect another 15–25 min.

I could cut it by running fewer synthetic seeds (e.g. 2 instead of 3, about a third fewer passes), but that means smaller n on the synthetic set. I'd rather let it finish. A background wait is set, and I'll post the false-positive rates as soon as it lands.
